description:
Is it ever okay to put a price on a kidney? Why is it illegal to sell an organ, but perfectly legal to sell blood plasma? This episode explores the world of "repugnant transactions"— the markets we find morally offensive — and asks why we ban certain markets as "gross" or "unethical" while ignoring others that might cause more harm.

Subscribe to our channel! http://goo.gl/0bsAjO

In this episode of The Gray Area, host Bryan Walsh sits down with Nobel laureate Alvin Roth, who wrote the recent book Moral Economics, to discuss how markets are the key to understanding our most deeply held social values. They break down why society chooses to ban certain transactions, how those choices affect real lives, and whether we can use "market design" to save people without violating our ethical standards.

description:
Public education funding doesn't always cover the costs for classroom supplies. To compensate, teachers create school supply wish lists or pay out of pocket for them so students have the tools they need to learn. Nevada's per-student funding is about $3K less than the estimated national average, but hope may be on the horizon for teachers and students.
